title: Reuse and Reuse
summary: A web server leaks a backup full of password hashes. Crack one, and the same password opens an account on a second server, where a careless program hands you root.
story: Birchwood Rentals (made up) runs two servers on 10.10.8.0/24: a public web server, web01, and an application server, app02. You start on scout.
goal: Capture the user flag and the root flag on app02.
skills: web recon, cracking sha512-crypt hashes, password reuse, a set-user-ID program

hints.text: Scan 10.10.8.0/24. web01 (10.10.8.20) runs a web server; app02 (10.10.8.30) runs ssh. Use webscan on web01 to find a folder it forgot: a backups folder is a good sign.
web01 serves /backups/accounts.bak, a file of user:hash lines ($6$..., sha512-crypt). Save it and run hashcrack on it: hashcrack accounts.bak
The renter password you cracked is reused on app02: ssh renter@10.10.8.30. Then find a set-user-ID program (find / -perm -4000) that reads files as root.
